## Why standard dosing fails

Time above MIC is the driver for beta-lactams, and three things move it:

- **renal function** — augmented clearance shortens the time above MIC
- **infusion duration** — extending the infusion raises trough exposure at
  the same daily dose
- **the organism's MIC** — the target moves with the pathogen

The next slides let us change each one and watch attainment respond.

---

## Attainment versus MIC

Standard 0.5 h infusion, 4 g q6h, normal renal function:

<iframe src="mipd-lab.html?mode=widget&panel=pta&summary=0&controls=0&model=pip_kim2022&dose=4000&tau=6&tinf=0.5&mic=16&target=ft100&n=800&seed=1"

::: {.fragment}

## Augmented renal clearance {background-iframe="mipd-lab.html?mode=widget&model=pip_udy2015&dose=4000&tau=6&tinf=0.33&mic=16&target=ft100&crcl=170&n=800&title=Unbound%20piperacillin,%20CLcr%20170%20mL/min" background-interactive="true"}

::: {.notes}
Udy's unbound-piperacillin model. Drop CLcr from 170 to 60 in the control
strip and the same regimen goes from failing to attaining.
:::

---

## Meropenem: does the dialysis modality change the dose? {background-iframe="mipd-lab.html?mode=widget&model=mem_ojeanson2021&dose=1000&tau=8&tinf=0.5&mic=2&target=ft100&dialysis=semicont&rd=200&n=800&title=Meropenem%201%20g%20q8h%20%E2%80%94%20100%25%20fT%3EMIC" background-interactive="true"}

::: {.notes}
O'Jeanson's model makes clearance a step function of modality: 11.0 L/h on
intermittent dialysis, 6.38 L/h on continuous. Switch the modality select
and the class sees attainment move without any dose changing — the point
being that "renal replacement therapy" is not one covariate value.
:::

---

## Cefepime in VAP: does prolonging the infusion rescue MIC 8? {background-iframe="mipd-lab.html?mode=widget&model=cef_nicasio2009&dose=2000&tau=8&tinf=3&mic=8&target=ft50&n=800&title=Cefepime%202%20g%20q8h%20%E2%80%94%2050%25%20fT%3EMIC" background-interactive="true"}

::: {.notes}
Nicasio's nonparametric VAP model. Drag the infusion duration from 3 h
back to 0.5 h and attainment at MIC 8 collapses; this is the comparison
the paper was built to make. Note the line beneath the plot reporting the
rejected fraction of covariance draws — a good moment to explain why a
nonparametric model cannot simply be sampled as a normal.
:::

---

## What does a loading dose buy? {background-iframe="mipd-lab.html?mode=widget&preset=van-load&n=800&panel=conc&title=Vancomycin%201%20g%20q12h%2C%20with%20and%20without%20a%202%20g%20load" background-interactive="true"}

::: {.notes}
Identical maintenance dosing in both arms. The only difference is a 2 g
load at t = 0, with maintenance starting 12 h later.

Ask the class to predict what happens to steady-state attainment before
revealing the table. The answer is nothing: 53.6% vs 53.7%. The plateau
is set by dose rate and clearance, so a loading dose cannot change it.

What it changes is day 1 — attainment 1.6% to 69.4%, and the fraction of
patients reaching AUC 400 within 24 h from 1.6% to 73.6%. For vancomycin
this matters more than it looks, because the 400-600 target is defined on
AUC(0-24): the day-1 column IS the target, not a proxy for it.

The corollary is worth stating explicitly: a loading dose buys time, never
exposure. It does not rescue an inadequate maintenance dose.
:::

## Why once daily? {background-iframe="mipd-lab.html?mode=widget&preset=gen-od&n=800&title=Gentamicin%20420%20mg%2Fday%2C%20three%20intervals" background-interactive="true"}

::: {.notes}
Identical daily dose, three intervals, one model (Xuan 2004, built
entirely on once-daily dosing). The joint target is Cmax/MIC >= 10 **and**
trough <= 2 mg/L, scored on the same simulated patient.

The separation is almost all in the PEAK component: 100% at q24h against
roughly 10% at q8h. AUC is unchanged across the three — so this is not a
dose-intensity effect, it is entirely the shape of the profile. Ask the
room which component they expected to move.
:::

## The same dose at CLcr 45 {background-iframe="mipd-lab.html?mode=widget&preset=gen-renal&n=800&title=Gentamicin%20in%20renal%20impairment" background-interactive="true"}

::: {.notes}
Same 420 mg q24h regimen, now in a 70-year-old with SCr 1.5 mg/dL. It
fails — and it fails on the TROUGH, with the peak still at 100%.

Two candidate fixes are on the plot. Extending to q48h keeps the peak
intact and recovers the trough. Halving the dose instead gives up peak
attainment as well and recovers the trough less. That asymmetry is the
whole argument for extending the interval rather than cutting the dose,
and it is visible in the component breakdown rather than having to be
asserted.
:::

## Amikacin: the peak has to move {background-iframe="mipd-lab.html?mode=widget&preset=amk-icu&n=800&title=Amikacin%20in%20a%20septic%20ICU%20patient" background-interactive="true"}

::: {.notes}
Romano 1998, a medical-ICU model whose covariates are categorical: trauma
raises clearance by 22.5%, sepsis raises the volume of distribution by
24.6%. Toggle the sepsis box live and watch the peak fall as the volume
expands.

At MIC 4, Cmax/MIC >= 10 needs 40 mg/L, and 1 g once daily does not get
there. This is the dose-escalation argument for amikacin, and the trough
ceiling (5 mg/L for amikacin, not 2) is what bounds it.
:::

## How the embedding works

Put `mipd-lab.html` beside the `.qmd` and declare it as a resource:

``` yaml
resources:
  - mipd-lab.html
```

Then either embed it inline —

``` html
<iframe src="mipd-lab.html?mode=widget&model=pip_kim2022&dose=4000&tau=6&tinf=4&mic=16&target=ft100"
        width="100%" height="440" style="border:0"></iframe>
```

— or make it the whole slide, which is the version to use when you want the
class driving it:

``` markdown
## Title {background-iframe="mipd-lab.html?mode=widget&..." background-interactive="true"}
```

::: {.notes}
`background-interactive="true"` is what lets clicks and typing reach the
widget instead of being swallowed by reveal.js navigation.
:::

---

## Reproducibility

Every widget URL carries `seed`, so the curve on the slide is the curve
that renders in the lecture theatre — and the same URL reproduces the
figure months later.

The file is self-contained: no CDN, no network, no server. It runs from a
USB stick.

```{=html}
<!-- Self-check: if mipd-lab.html is not sitting beside this deck, every
     widget slide renders blank (reveal.js shows the iframe's 404 page).
     This probes for the app once and replaces a silent blank with an
     actionable message. -->
<div id="mipd-missing" style="display:none;position:fixed;inset:auto 0 0 0;z-index:99;
     background:#b4232a;color:#fff;font:14px/1.5 -apple-system,Segoe UI,Roboto,sans-serif;
     padding:14px 18px">
  <b>The dosing widget could not be loaded.</b><br>
  <code style="background:rgba(255,255,255,.18);padding:1px 5px;border-radius:3px">mipd-lab.html</code>
  must sit in the same folder as <code style="background:rgba(255,255,255,.18);padding:1px 5px;border-radius:3px">slides-demo.qmd</code>
  before you render. Copy it there, re-render, and this message disappears.
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  var probe = document.createElement('iframe');
  probe.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;opacity:0;border:0;left:-9999px';
  var settled = false;
  function verdict(missing) {
    if (settled) return;
    settled = true;
    if (missing) document.getElementById('mipd-missing').style.display = 'block';
    if (probe.parentNode) probe.parentNode.removeChild(probe);
  }
  probe.onload = function () {
    // A 404 page loads successfully, so presence of the app's own global is
    // the test — not the load event. Cross-origin access throws under
    // file:// in some browsers; in that case assume the file is fine rather
    // than cry wolf.
    var ok;
    try { ok = !!probe.contentWindow.PKPD; } catch (e) { ok = true; }
    verdict(!ok);
  };
  probe.onerror = function () { verdict(true); };
  probe.src = 'mipd-lab.html?mode=widget&n=20';
  document.body.appendChild(probe);
  setTimeout(function () { verdict(false); }, 8000);
})();
</script>
```
